question.text: Under Rule 8(4) of the PML Rules, where a reporting entity delays in reporting a transaction or in rectifying a mis-reported transaction beyond the specified time limit, how is the default treated for the purpose of penalty?

answer.text: Each day of delay constitutes a separate violation
Each week of delay constitutes a separate violation
Each month of delay constitutes a separate violation
The entire period of delay is treated as a single violation

explanation.text: The Logic: Rule 8(4) provides that delay of each day in not reporting a transaction, or in rectifying a mis-reported transaction, beyond the time limit specified in Rule 8 constitutes a separate violation. The penalty therefore accumulates on a daily basis. The Trap: Weekly, monthly, or single-event counting would significantly reduce the penalty impact and is not what Rule 8(4) prescribes; the daily-violation mechanism is what creates the deterrent for delayed or mis-reported transactions. Note: Rule 8(4) is specifically about delay in transaction reporting or in rectifying a mis-reported transaction beyond the Rule 8 time limit, rather than a general "failure to furnish information or records" rule.
